environment_strategy: Pinned external checkout under third_party/checkouts/hifirepoqa (gitignored, never committed to ANT's own repo -- see .gitignore's third_party/checkouts/ entry), with its own isolated venv (.venv, Python 3.13, `pip install requests tqdm` -- tree_sitter_languages requested but NOT installable in this environment, no matching wheel found for this platform/Python combination; the code's own try/except around that import falls back to Python's stdlib ast module, so this degrades multi-language symbol extraction to Python-only rather than failing outright -- a real, disclosed limitation of THIS session's setup, not of the method).
execution_status: VERIFIED LIVE, PARTIALLY -- NOT a completed end-to-end question. A real run against qibo (commit-pinned to 2f98679c4a738d5a59de17eccd4712659d52a461, the exact commit ANT/Matched ReAct/Retrieval evaluate against in this session's regression smoke -- confirmed via `git rev-parse HEAD` match) confirmed: (1) the pinned checkout clones correctly to the exact requested commit; (2) real GPT-4.1 chat-completion calls succeed against the real OpenAI API; (3) real embedding calls reach the real OpenAI API (some succeeded, many hit 429). Did NOT reach a final synthesized answer within this session's time budget -- see 'known_cost_characteristic' below. A second attempt hit a Windows-specific `shutil.rmtree` WinError 5 (Access is denied) on a git pack .idx file during clone_repository()'s always-delete-and-reclone step -- likely a transient file-lock (antivirus scan or a lingering handle from the prior clone), not investigated further given time constraints; may not reproduce on Linux/Mac.
known_cost_characteristic: HiFiRepoQA's own knowledge-base-building step (summary_functions/summary_classes) summarizes EVERY function and class found anywhere in the target repository via one LLM call each, with NO rate-limit backoff/retry logic in the released code. Measured directly against qibo (419 files eligible under this suite's own EvalRepoEnvironment policy): 1483 functions found needing summarization. At the observed pace (heavily degraded by sustained 429 'Too Many Requests' against OpenAI's standard rate limits -- no backoff means every 429 is simply logged and moved past with a zero-value embedding, not retried), this was on pace for multiple hours for ONE repo's first-time build. This is a genuine, disclosed, METHOD-INHERENT cost -- the DAG/Planning/Retrieval/Analysis/Synthesis architecture legitimately requires this whole-repo pre-index before answering even one question -- not an implementation defect to route around by limiting scope (which would violate this suite's own 'do not erase method-specific components' rule). The per-function/class summary cache IS incremental and keyed by repo_name (verified in source: load_existing_summaries()/processed_functions set skips already-done work on a subsequent run against the same repo_name) -- so a SECOND question against an already-indexed repo should be far cheaper/faster than the first. Budgeting real wall-clock/cost for a formal run must account for this per-repo, one-time cost explicitly -- not assume per-question costs are uniform the way they are for ANT/Matched ReAct/Retrieval.
local_modifications: config.py: DEFAULT_CONFIG['api_provider'] changed from 'xxx' (not a key in API_CONFIGS, which only defines 'gpt-4o') to 'gpt-4o'. As released, `import config`'s own module-level `default_config = Config.get_config()` statement crashed unconditionally with ValueError('Unknown API provider: xxx') at IMPORT TIME -- before any REPO_QA_* environment variable override could run. This is not an agent-logic change; REPO_QA_API_KEY/URL/MODEL_NAME (via load_env_config(), itself unmodified) still override the placeholder credentials exactly as originally designed.

repo_qa_agent.py get_embedding(): added REPO_QA_EMBEDDING_URL/REPO_QA_EMBEDDING_MODEL/REPO_QA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY env-var overrides (falling back to the original, non-functional placeholder -- 'https://xxx.com/v1/embeddings', model 'qwen-embedding', no auth header -- unchanged when unset). As released this call could never succeed against any real service; this mirrors exactly how the chat-completion trio (REPO_QA_API_KEY/URL/MODEL_NAME) already works, extended to the one call site that was never parameterized.

repo_qa_agent.py clone_repository()/RetrievalAgent.clone_repo(): added an optional `commit` parameter. As released, cloning is ALWAYS a shallow (--depth 1) clone of the current default-branch HEAD with no way to pin an older commit -- a real reproducibility gap against a benchmark whose questions are written against a fixed commit_id. When `commit` is provided, this does a full (non-shallow) clone instead (a shallow clone's history doesn't contain older commits, so checking one out afterward would fail) then `git checkout <commit>`. Threaded from a new `issue_data['commit_id']` field this wrapper's own input record now includes. Verified live: resulting checkout's HEAD matched the pinned commit_id exactly.

_ant_driver.py (new file, checkout root, NOT part of the official release): calls RepoQAMultiAgent.process_issue() directly, reading one JSON record from stdin and writing the result dict to stdout as JSON -- avoids main.py's own hardcoded input_path/output_dir string literals (main() reads from a literal '/path/to/your/input/data' with no CLI args) without needing to patch main.py itself. Config resolution (Config.get_config() + load_env_config()) is used completely unmodified inside this driver.
